articles.title: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules
articles.summary: The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules
articles.summaryTr: The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins.
articles.articleText: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins. Opinion by Lissele Pratt, co-founder, Capitalixe Last weekend, the Federal Bureau of Investigation claimed that North Korea was behind the $6.3 billion Binance hack, which analysts are calling the largest heist on record. While I’ve read a lot about the scale of this heist, far less has been said about what went right. Because while it is true that the perpetrators stole $6.3 billion, they haven’t actually been able to hold on to a significant proportion of those takings. $2.85 billion of the funds has been frozen. The reason for this comes down to what the stolen money was comprised of. Of that $2.85 billion, 94% was held in stablecoins. While this hack was terrible news all around, it did show that centralized control, oftentimes criticized by crypto purists, might actually be one of the strongest tools we have against crypto crime. Because, unlike other assets, stablecoins can be frozen by their issuers, giving victims a real chance to stop stolen money reaching the wrong hands. It does, however, raise an uncomfortable question. If private companies have the power to freeze billions of dollars in assets, who decides when they should be allowed to use it? The United Kingdom now has the opportunity to do just that. The race to get rid of stablecoins To get an idea of just how much the freeze mattered, you just have to look at what the hackers did within the first hour of their heist. Related: Binance, Polymarket seek Polygon hard fork to recover $6.8M in stolen crypto Clearly, they understood that there was a very limited window to move the stablecoins before anyone could stop them. So that’s exactly what they did. What was frozen from the Binance hack. Source: Elliptic Less than an hour after the hack began, they had already sold $325 million worth of stolen USDT (Tether’s stablecoin) for Ether. The reasoning behind this was to swap an asset that could be frozen with one that could not. Luckily, stablecoin issuers were quick to act, with Tether’s first major freeze coming just 37 minutes after the stolen funds reached the hackers’ main wallet, and Circle following three minutes later, blocking the movement of USDC. Without Tether and Circle intervening, far more of the funds could have ended up beyond their reach. We’re yet to agree on the rules The freeze, to its credit, worked for the most part because a handful of companies decided, in real time, to use it. The problem is that there still isn’t an agreed standard that outlines when a freeze is justified or how quickly the response needs to be, and we’re beginning to see the consequences of not having these answers. For instance, Circle is facing a proposed class action from Drift Protocol investors who allege it failed to freeze around $230 million in stolen USDC after the April hack. Their argument is that Circle could have stopped the money from moving, but didn’t act in time. Meanwhile, Tether is being sued in New York by two businessmen who claim it froze millions of their assets months before a seizure warrant existed. It’s important to mention that Tether has responded to this case, calling these allegations baseless. Working in payments and banking, it’s not uncommon for me to see traditional banks freeze money and accounts. Due to this, you may argue that if a bank can do this frequently, why shouldn’t a stablecoin issuer be able to? Stablecoin freeze timeline. Source: CertiK My argument isn’t that they shouldn’t. But banks don’t get to decide they want to freeze assets out of nowhere. There’s usually a legal trigger behind their decision, as well as a way to challenge it. Stablecoin issuers now hold the same power while having to act faster and across borders. So it’s about time they’re given some structure. Britain can fix this There is, however, a caveat with regulating stablecoin issuers. Tether and Circle, two of the largest issuers, aren’t based in the UK, so British regulators can’t simply tell them what to do. Related: Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool What Britain can control, though, is which stablecoins UK customers are allowed to buy, and they’ve already begun doing so. In June, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) published its cryptoassets regime. Under it, UK trading platforms must carry out due diligence and publish a disclosure document before they list a coin, and that includes stablecoins issued overseas. It comes into force on 25 October 2027. The Bank of England is finalizing its Code of Practice for systemic stablecoin issuers by the end of this year. It covers stablecoins used widely enough for payments to matter to UK financial stability. Neither framework establishes the clear obligations around freezing stolen funds that I believe are necessary. But both are still taking shape, giving the UK the perfect opportunity to address this gap now, rather than trying to retrofit new requirements later. Two conditions for a UK listing So here’s a solution that I believe would work. Before a stablecoin can be sold on a UK platform, its issuer should have to agree to two conditions. The first being that it is contactable and ready to act. Tether and Circle did exactly that last week, but the victim was the world’s biggest exchange. A small UK platform should get the same response. I work with a number of smaller crypto businesses that don’t have Binance’s profile or a direct line to Tether. Under the current system, they’re the ones most likely to be left waiting. The second is that there needs to be a clear timetable for what happens next. If an issuer freezes funds, it should notify the National Crime Agency that same day. The freeze should then expire if there hasn’t been a court order put out to keep the wallet frozen. Neither of these are extremely controversial takes. They’d give law enforcement a chance to intervene when money is stolen and also protect people from having their assets frozen indefinitely, without legal grounds. The Binance hack has shown us that stablecoins can give victims of crypto crime a chance to stop stolen money before it’s gone for good. That shouldn’t be a privilege reserved only for the world’s biggest exchanges. Magazine: Can decentralized phone networks power the AI revolution?

articles.articleText: Strategy buys 1,036 Bitcoin as BTC holdings climb to 850,364 Strategy bought $81.9 million in Bitcoin last week while spending $188.3 million repurchasing STRC preferred shares, according to its latest SEC filing. Strategy bought 1,036 Bitcoin for $81.9 million last week, bringing its holdings to 850,364 BTC. The company paid an average of $79,012 per BTC last week, according to its Monday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Strategy said it paid a total of $64.16 billion for its Bitcoin holdings, at an average price of $75,456 per coin. Its holdings now account for roughly 4.05% of Bitcoin’s maximum 21 million supply. articles.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

articles.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
articles.articleText: Release Number 9315-26 CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws. The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law. “Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.” This action reflects the CFTC’s firm commitment to maintaining its exclusive jurisdiction over CFTC-registered prediction markets. The CFTC continues to draw a clear line: if a state challenges the lawful operation of a derivatives exchange, the Commission will protect federal sovereign interests. The Commission has also initiated legal proceedings against nine other states and has submitted briefs in four federal courts of appeal and one state supreme court. -CFTC-

news.summary: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.

news.titleTr: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
news.summaryTr: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
news.articleText: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud - Published A civil servant who secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud. Kashim Chowdhury, from east London, had five government jobs that overlapped in the spring of 2023. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money. The prosecution accused the 56-year-old of ''deliberate, intentional dishonesty'' and of ''exploiting the system''. After seven hours of deliberation, the jury unanimously found Chowdhury guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by a failure to disclose. The judge said Chowdhury faced a ''very significant custodial sentence''. He added he was refusing bail because of the significance of the crime and for Chowdhury's own wellbeing. 'Abused trust' "This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty," said Sarah Melo, specialist prosecutor at the CPS Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate. "He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing." A Defra spokesperson said Chowdury "abused the trust placed in him as a public servant", adding that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending. Between 2020 and 2023 Chowdhury had eight full-time public sector roles that overlapped and earned him £350,000 in total. The prosecution told the court that on application forms he provided inaccurate information about his employment status and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already a civil servant. Once he secured the roles he didn't tell his employers he was working elsewhere. He was allowed to work entirely from home because he told his employers he was caring for his mother, whom he lived with in east London. She had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. But rather than reduce his workload to look after her, he kept taking on new jobs. In the spring of 2023, when his mother was a few months away from death, he had jobs at the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days. Chowdhury said he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment in the past. He was made redundant from a job at the Department for Education in 2013 and was given a diagnosis of PTSD. He said he had not been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time". But the prosecution barrister, Lucy Organ, told the jury: "He's lied to you in evidence, he's lied to you under oath, which demonstrates the level of deceit he has descended to." A succession of his managers told the court about his poor performance. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time". McCartney said that during video calls Chowdhury had his camera switched off blaming technical problems. McCartney said this went on for four to five months. But McCartney said that because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job and remained there for two years. The prosecution argued that he used sick notes to cope with his impossible schedule. In March 2023, he was on sick leave from four of the organisations he worked for. But he kept working at the Home Office and did not tell them he was ill. His line manager at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023. By this point he'd been off sick for three months and she wanted to make a plan to get him back to work. She told the jury that at the start of the call he was coughing a lot and waving tissues up to the camera. She also told the jury that he had been wearing white make-up to try to look ill. Adams told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck." Chowdhury told the jury this was a smear and that he had not been wearing make-up. After the call, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it he blamed a technical error. Adams grew suspicious. ''I believed he was lying,'' she told the jury. She escalated her concerns up the chain at the UKHSA. But his fraudulent behaviour went on for several more months until he left the civil service in September 2023. He was finally caught in 2024 by the government's National Fraud Initiative, which conducts searches of civil service databases such as payroll every two years to look for anomalies. Chowdhury has also been accused by his siblings of bullying their mother into increasing his share of the family home days before she died. In a case at the High Court, Chowdhury's two brothers and sister allege that he put "undue influence" on Faijun Nessa to sign documents that meant he would inherit half of her home. The four-storey, six-bedroom home in east London has been valued at £2.1m. His siblings say their mother could not have understood what she was signing because she was "desperately unwell". In January 2023 she was given a terminal diagnosis of stage four metastatic colorectal cancer. The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed. Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing.

news.title: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results
news.summary: Trump made the claims, without evidence, on Truth Social on Monday.

news.titleTr: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results
news.summaryTr: Trump made the claims, without evidence, on Truth Social on Monday.
news.articleText: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results - Published US President Donald Trump has questioned the legitimacy of the midterm election results in which Republicans suffered sweeping losses - days after saying he would accept the outcome. "Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong?" Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday. This appeared to contradict what he told the New York Times on election night that he was "absolutely willing" to accept the results. Democrats retook both chambers of Congress in last week's elections. State and local officials across the US said voting had been mostly problem-free. Some key races, including Senate contests in Alaska and Mississippi, have yet to be called. In the Truth Social post, Trump made vague claims about polling, voting "dumps", and "machines" without providing specific evidence of error or wrongdoing. He has previously attempted to cast doubts on the integrity of elections he has lost, although he himself was not on the ballot in the midterms. "We would have won easily if I was on the ballot," Trump told CBS News, the BBC's US partner, after it was confirmed his party had lost both the Senate and the House. As it stands, Democrats have won 54 US Senate seats and 254 US House seats in the midterms, giving them comfortable majorities in both chambers of Congress even as counting continues in some races. The outcome has been clear since election night and Trump told the New York Times then: "We'll, you know, look forward to working with [Democrats]", adding: "We'll probably work something out." He has also offered his own analysis of why Republicans lost, acknowledging on Fox News that the Iran war had contributed to the defeat. "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran but they really probably weren't willing to do the short term consequences of paying more for gasoline - I understand that," he said. Vice-President JD Vance has also blamed the Iran war, which began in February and which has severely disrupted global oil and gas supplies - causing costs to soar, as the reason their party lost the election. In the run-up to the midterms, Trump made claims about widespread voting fraud, despite evidence that it is rare. He and his allies alleged for months that the 2020 presidential election, which he lost to former President Joe Biden, had been rigged against him. His lawyers and allies spent weeks attempting to litigate the results, but courts repeatedly struck them down. The justice department during his administration has made unprecedented attempts to exert more federal control over elections - a power the Constitution primarily delegates to individual states. Days before these midterms, it filed controversial lawsuits in federal courts challenging the count and certification of votes in states like California and Alaska, but judges ruled against them in nearly all instances. Election law experts, state officials, and local elections offices told the BBC they had spent months preparing for a scenario in which the White House or election sceptics questioned the votes' legitimacy. Despite the intense focus around election integrity on both sides of the debate, top state and local election officials have reported a mostly smooth process so far for the 2026 midterms. Extreme weather did force some location closures, and a handful of reported administrative or technical issues slowed the process in some local jurisdictions.

news.articleText: Pegasus'un (PGSUS) 3. çeyrekte beklentileri aştı: İşte bilanço detayları! - Pegasus, 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde 11,27 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Ancak yılın ilk yarısındaki zarar nedeniyle şirketin 9 aylık toplam net sonucu 1,28 milyar TL zarar oldu. Üçüncü çeyrek kârı piyasa beklentilerini aştı. Pegasus Hava Taşımacılığı A.Ş. (PGSUS), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 9 Kasım'da Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, 1 Ocak-30 Eylül 2026 döneminde 1 milyar 279 milyon 203 bin TL net zarar açıkladı. Pegasus, 2025'in aynı döneminde 13 milyar 326 milyon 666 bin TL net kâr elde etmişti. Buna karşın şirket, yalnızca 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde 11 milyar 272 milyon 632 bin TL net kâr kaydetti. Satış gelirleri yüzde 32 arttı Pegasus'un ilk 9 aylık hasılatı, geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki 114 milyar 405 milyon 95 bin TL'den 150 milyar 626 milyon 803 bin TL'ye yükseldi. Böylece satış gelirlerinde yıllık bazda yüzde 32 artış gerçekleşti. Şirketin esas faaliyet kârı ise aynı dönemde 10 milyar 872 milyon 782 bin TL'den 9 milyar 359 milyon 283 bin TL'ye geriledi. FAVÖK, 2025'in ilk 9 ayında 30 milyar 246 milyon 178 bin TL seviyesindeyken, 2026'nın aynı döneminde 26 milyar 518 milyon 410 bin TL olarak gerçekleşti. Pegasus'un varlıkları 492 milyar TL'yi aştı Şirketin toplam varlıkları 2025 yıl sonundaki 410 milyar 168 milyon 212 bin TL'den 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreği sonunda 492 milyar 104 milyon 652 bin TL'ye yükseldi. Aynı dönemde toplam borçlar 293 milyar 314 milyon 340 bin TL'den 360 milyar 369 milyon 107 bin TL'ye çıktı. Özkaynaklar ise 116 milyar 853 milyon 872 bin TL'den 131 milyar 735 milyon 545 bin TL'ye ulaştı. Pegasus'un piyasa değeri 73,25 milyar TL, PD/DD oranı ise 0,56 olarak açıklandı. Pegasus bilançosu beklentileri aştı Matriks Haber tarafından gerçekleştirilen bilanço anketine 15 aracı kurum katıldı. Ankete göre Pegasus'un üçüncü çeyrek net kârına ilişkin ortalama beklenti 8 milyar 895 milyon 300 bin TL, medyan beklenti ise 8 milyar 834 milyon TL oldu. Şirketin açıkladığı 11 milyar 272 milyon 632 bin TL'lik üçüncü çeyrek net kârı, hem ortalama hem de medyan beklentinin üzerinde gerçekleşti.

news.summary: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.

news.titleTr: Nine Zimbabweans caught allegedly trying to leave South Africa to fight in Ukraine
news.summaryTr: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.
news.articleText: Nine Zimbabweans caught allegedly trying to leave South Africa to fight in Ukraine - Published Nine Zimbabweans have been arrested in South Africa after they were caught allegedly trying to leave the country to fight in the war between Russia and the Ukraine, police say. The group, aged between 20 and 26, were arrested in and around Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team on Sunday evening. They were caught as they were "preparing to board flights out of the country", authorities added, but their final destination is unclear. They have been charged with contravening South Africa's Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act, which outlaws mercenary activity without government permission. Police said five people were arrested at South Africa's biggest airport, OR Tambo, and another four at a hotel in Bruma, east of Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team that involved Interpol. All nine later appeared in court, according to state prosecutors. The police statement added that the involvement of Interpol and other international law enforcement agencies indicated that the suspects had also allegedly violated laws in their respective home countries, prompting cooperation with South African authorities. They have also not said whether the group allegedly intended to fight for Russia or Ukraine nor provided details of the organisations allegedly involved in facilitating their travel. Citizens of several African countries, including Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, have gone to fight for Russia in Ukraine - some they had been duped and had not realised where they were going. A Ukrainian intelligence assessment estimated earlier this year that more than 1,700 people from 36 countries in Africa have been recruited to fight for Russia. Kenya at the time estimated that 252 citizens had been illegally conscripted in Russia. In March, Foreign Minister Musalia Mudavadi visited Moscow to address the issue. He said at the time that an agreement had been reached to stop recruiting Kenyan nationals. In March, Zimbabwe said that 15 of its nationals had been killed after being recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine, with more than 60 still trapped on the frontlines. The previous month, South Africa secured the return of 17 South Africans who were allegedly tricked into joining the war. In December last year, South African authorities arrested five people, including a journalist, for allegedly recruiting people to join the war. Ukraine has also been recruiting foreign nationals, including from Africa. news.title: Men recruited to French gang as children to kill give rare insight into drug underworld
news.summary: "It destroys people, but we all make our own choices" - Marseille drug-gang members spoke to the BBC.

news.titleTr: Men recruited to French gang as children to kill give rare insight into drug underworld
news.summaryTr: "It destroys people, but we all make our own choices" - Marseille drug-gang members spoke to the BBC.
news.articleText: Men recruited to French gang as children to kill give rare insight into drug underworld A BBC investigation has found one of Europe's most powerful drug gangs in France is recruiting teenage children from across the country to commit kidnap and murder. Known as the "DZ Mafia", the gang won a bloody turf war against a rival group in Marseille during 2023, and is now recruiting from further afield. One member who is in prison awaiting trial after being implicated in several murders told the BBC he was part of a DZ Mafia hit squad. He agrees the killings he has been charged with were "quite shocking". "Attempts in broad daylight, in traffic jams… it can range from going to hit a guy, slap him to taking him in front of his mother and burning him up in a car. I think I have good composure, I handle it fairly well." When challenged over whether he feels regret when carrying out such acts of brutality, he says he feels "guilty in-part" but claims to have no regrets. Like so many teenagers from Marseille, he knew large sums of money could be earned quickly in drug trafficking. Now in his twenties, he admits the environment he entered was a "trap". The BBC's Paris Correspondent, James Waterhouse, reports from Marseille.

news.summaryTr: Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan, fon soruşturmasına ilişkin “Taviz yok” mesajı verirken emeklilerin durumunu iyileştirecek mali imkanlar üzerinde çalışıldığını söyledi. news.articleText: Erdoğan'dan emekli maaşları için yeni mesaj: “Mali imkanları oluşturuyoruz” - Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan, fon soruşturmasına ilişkin “Taviz yok” mesajı verirken emeklilerin durumunu iyileştirecek mali imkanlar üzerinde çalışıldığını söyledi. Gabar'da iki yeni sahadan daha olumlu haber geldiğini belirten Erdoğan, petrol üretimi ve enerji hedeflerine ilişkin açıklamalarda bulundu. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan başkanlığında gerçekleştirilen Kabine toplantısının ardından ekonomi gündemine ilişkin açıklamalar yapıldı. Erdoğan, fon soruşturmasının yakından takip edildiğini belirtirken emekli aylıklarına yönelik yeni düzenleme çalışmalarına ve Gabar'daki petrol faaliyetlerine de değindi. Fon soruşturmasında “taviz yok” mesajı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan, fon soruşturmasına ilişkin sürecin yakından takip edildiğini belirterek, “Meseleyi çok sıkı bir şekilde takip ediyoruz. Vatandaşlarımız bize güvenmeye devam etsin” ifadelerini kullandı. Erdoğan'ın açıklaması, soruşturmanın kararlılıkla sürdürüleceği mesajı olarak öne çıktı. Emekli maaşlarına ek zam hazırlığı Kabine toplantısının gündeminde emekli aylıklarına yönelik düzenleme de yer aldı. Erdoğan, emeklilerin ekonomik durumunu iyileştirmeye yönelik çalışmalar hakkında, “Emeklilerimizin durumunu biraz daha iyileştirecek mali imkanları oluşturuyoruz” dedi. Emeklilere enflasyon farkının yanı sıra ek refah payı verilmesine yönelik çalışmalar sürüyor. Hazırlanan taslakların Erdoğan'a sunulmasının ardından düzenlemenin bütçe süreciyle birlikte Meclis gündemine taşınması planlanıyor. Ancak emekli maaşlarına yapılacak olası ek zam oranı ve yeni maaş tutarlarına ilişkin henüz kesin bir rakam açıklanmadı. Gabar'da iki yeni sahadan petrol haberi Erdoğan, Türkiye'nin enerji arz güvenliği ve yerli kaynakların üretime kazandırılması konusunda atılan adımlara da değindi. Karadeniz'de üretilen doğal gazla 4 milyon hanenin ihtiyacının karşılandığını belirten Erdoğan, Osmangazi Gemisi'nin devreye alınmasıyla bu sayının 8 milyona çıkarılmasının hedeflendiğini söyledi. Gabar'daki petrol üretimine ilişkin de açıklamalarda bulunan Erdoğan, bölgede iki yeni sahadan daha olumlu haber geldiğini duyurdu. Gabar'da 75,4 milyon varil Türkiye'nin en kaliteli petrolünün üretildiğini ifade etti. Türkiye'nin enerji sepetini genişletmeye, yerli petrol ve doğal gaz kaynaklarını ekonomiye kazandırmaya yönelik çalışmaların sürdüğünü vurguladı.

news.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
news.summary: The cyber-attack last month saw fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France heated up.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
news.summaryTr: The cyber-attack last month saw fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France heated up.
news.articleText: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking - Published France has accused Iran of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of Iran. He said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding that the country would "implement sanctions at the European level against all those responsible for this attack". The cyber-attack last month saw fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France heated up, which spoilt fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros. Then last week, dozens of supermarkets across seven other European countries were also impacted by a cyber-attack that targeted fridges and freezers. It is not known if the instances are linked. Iran is yet to respond to Barrot's allegations. Barrot said of the attack on France's supermarkets: "It marks the first large-scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people." He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act". France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added. Separately on Monday, the Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as well as his two deputies. Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC. On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets. More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight. Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss. The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe. Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects. In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them. The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations. news.title: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
news.summary: The discount chain is continuing to edge towards collapse and is said to be "running on fumes", according to one insider.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
news.summaryTr: The discount chain is continuing to edge towards collapse and is said to be "running on fumes", according to one insider.
news.articleText: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow - Published Poundland is unable to buy new stock to fill its shelves after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts. The discount chain is on the brink of collapse with one insider describing it as "running on fumes". It has until Thursday to secure a rescue deal. About £50m has been frozen by its American owner Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning its 600 shops are running out of stock. Pressure is building on Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for £1 last June, after the owner rejected a takeover bid that could have saved the thousands of jobs currently at risk. Gordon Brothers has been approached for comment. Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its creditors until Thursday. Access to funds was limited because of a tension between Gordon Brothers' dual role as both creditor and shareholder, a source said, but added they expected a relaxation of funds in the next two days. Last week, Poundland boss Barry Williams told staff like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4% last week, which included Halloween, but said this was £1.5m ahead of budget. He said the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where the business made losses of £68m. The latest annual accounts have yet to be audited. - Burnham 'ready to support' Poundland staff as retailer faces collapse - Published29 October - Poundland staff protest after chain approach administrators - Published29 October However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture of the business, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading". It said it had provided significant funding to support the company's ability to trade since it acquired the business. It has also made £18m, from a combination of debt interest payments and other fees and charges. On Wednesday, executives from Gordon Brothers will appear before the Business Select Committee with MPs probing whether they are genuinely pursuing a solvent rescue of the business, which has 11,000 employees, and whether every realistic step is being taken to protect jobs and stores. The session is being held in private given commercially sensitive discussions are still under way with bidders. Uncertain future On Thursday, the 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended. If not, Poundland is set to collapse into administration and could be broken up. A source familiar with the sales process said London-based Xyra Group was making "significant progress" in its last minute bid to buy Poundland and could now be the front runner. An extension of Thursday's deadline now seems an increasingly likely scenario. But such a case would be difficult to put forward if Gordon Brothers continues to block funding. One observer remarked "if Gordon Brothers is going in front of that committee, you don't want to be giving the message we're pulling up the drawbridge". Even if a deal is agreed to sell the business as a whole, there is no guarantee a new owner would not reduce the number of stores, but suppliers to Poundland would prefer that outcome to hundreds of sites being sold off to other retailers. There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up stores which could mean continuing employment for many workers. The central issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland trading as a national chain.

He said the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where the business made losses of £68m. The latest annual accounts have yet to be audited. - Burnham 'ready to support' Poundland staff as retailer faces collapse - Published29 October - Poundland staff protest after chain approach administrators - Published29 October However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture of the business, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading". It said it had provided significant funding to support the company's ability to trade since it acquired the business. It has also made £18m, from a combination of debt interest payments and other fees and charges. On Wednesday, executives from Gordon Brothers will appear before the Business Select Committee with MPs probing whether they are genuinely pursuing a solvent rescue of the business, which has 11,000 employees, and whether every realistic step is being taken to protect jobs and stores. The session is being held in private given commercially sensitive discussions are still under way with bidders. Uncertain future On Thursday, the 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended. If not, Poundland is set to collapse into administration and could be broken up. A source familiar with the sales process said London-based Xyra Group was making "significant progress" in its last minute bid to buy Poundland and could now be the front runner. An extension of Thursday's deadline now seems an increasingly likely scenario. But such a case would be difficult to put forward if Gordon Brothers continues to block funding. One observer remarked "if Gordon Brothers is going in front of that committee, you don't want to be giving the message we're pulling up the drawbridge". Even if a deal is agreed to sell the business as a whole, there is no guarantee a new owner would not reduce the number of stores, but suppliers to Poundland would prefer that outcome to hundreds of sites being sold off to other retailers. There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up stores which could mean continuing employment for many workers. The central issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland trading as a national chain.

news.titleTr: Apple'dan Türkiye'ye 7 yeni merkez yatırımı! İlk açılış 2027'de
news.summaryTr: Apple, Türkiye'de beş ücretsiz geliştirici akademisi, İstanbul'da bir Developer Center ve Ankara'da bir üretim akademisi açacak. İlk merkezlerin 2027'de faaliyete geçmesi planlanıyor.
news.articleText: Apple'dan Türkiye'ye 7 yeni merkez yatırımı! İlk açılış 2027'de - Apple, Türkiye'de beş ücretsiz geliştirici akademisi, İstanbul'da bir Developer Center ve Ankara'da bir üretim akademisi açacak. İlk merkezlerin 2027'de faaliyete geçmesi planlanıyor. Teknoloji devi Apple, Türkiye'deki faaliyetlerini genişletmek amacıyla yedi yeni eğitim ve teknoloji merkezi kuracağını duyurdu. 9 Kasım'da açıklanan yatırım planı kapsamında Türkiye genelinde beş Apple Developer Academy, İstanbul'da bir Apple Developer Center ve Ankara'da bir Apple Manufacturing Academy açılacak. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Yazılım geliştirme, girişimcilik ve ileri üretim teknolojilerine odaklanacak merkezlerle Türkiye'deki yazılım geliştiricilerin desteklenmesi ve küçük ve orta ölçekli işletmelerin yapay zeka destekli üretim teknolojilerine erişiminin artırılması hedefleniyor. Apple, yatırımın toplam maliyetini açıklamadı. Şirketin takvimine göre ilk geliştirici akademisi ve İstanbul'daki geliştirici merkezi 2027'de, Ankara'daki üretim akademisi ise 2028'de faaliyete başlayacak. Türkiye'de beş ücretsiz geliştirici akademisi açılacak Apple, önümüzdeki üç yıl içinde Türkiye'nin farklı noktalarında beş Apple Developer Academy kurmayı planlıyor. İlk akademi 2027 yılında İstanbul'da açılacak. Diğer dört merkezin hangi şehirlerde kurulacağı henüz açıklanmadı. Akademilerde öğrencilere ve girişimcilere dokuz ay süren ücretsiz ve yoğun eğitim programları sunulacak. Eğitimlerde kodlama, uygulama tasarımı, pazarlama, proje yönetimi ve yapay zeka teknolojilerine odaklanılacak. Programlarda erişilebilirlik, kullanıcı gizliliği ve sürdürülebilirlik konuları da ele alınacak. Apple, akademilerden önümüzdeki yıllarda binlerce öğrencinin yararlanabileceğini belirtiyor. Ancak başvuru tarihleri, kabul koşulları ve kontenjanlar henüz duyurulmadı. İstanbul, Apple'ın geliştirici merkezleri arasına katılacak Apple, 2027 yılında İstanbul'da bir Apple Developer Center da açacak. Merkez, profesyonel yazılım geliştiricilere ve teknoloji girişimlerine yönelik hizmet verecek. Geliştiriciler burada Apple uzmanlarıyla birlikte çalışma, yeni teknolojileri deneyimleme ve uygulamalarını geliştirme imkanı bulacak. Yüz yüze eğitimler, teknik atölyeler, bire bir uzman görüşmeleri ve geliştirici etkinlikleri düzenlenecek. İstanbul'daki merkez, Apple'ın Bengaluru, Berlin, Cupertino, Şanghay ve Singapur'da bulunan geliştirici merkezleri ağına katılacak. Ankara'da yapay zeka ve robotik akademisi kurulacak Yatırım planının üretim teknolojilerine yönelik ayağı ise Ankara'da hayata geçirilecek. 2028 yılında açılması planlanan Apple Manufacturing Academy, Apple'ın ABD dışındaki ilk üretim akademisi olacak. Merkezde özellikle küçük ve orta ölçekli işletmelere yönelik ücretsiz eğitimler verilecek. Programların odağında yapay zeka, makine öğrenmesi, gelişmiş otomasyon, robotik sistemler ve tahmine dayalı bakım teknolojileri bulunacak. Akademide uygulamalı eğitim laboratuvarları, teknoloji gösterimleri, ortak çalışma alanları ve profesyonel gelişim etkinlikleri de yer alacak. Ankara'daki tesisin bir üretim fabrikası olmayacağının altını çizmek gerekiyor. Merkez, Apple cihazlarının üretileceği bir tesis değil; Türkiye'deki işletmelerin ileri üretim teknolojileri konusunda eğitim ve destek alabileceği bir akademi olarak tasarlandı. Tim Cook: Türkiye'deki girişimcileri destekleyeceğiz Apple Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Tim Cook, Türkiye'deki yatırım planına ilişkin açıklamasında şirketin 35 yıldır Türkiye'deki müşterilerine ve topluluklara hizmet verdiğini hatırlattı. Türkiye'deki yazılım geliştiricilerin dünya genelinde kullanılan uygulamalar ürettiğine dikkat çeken Cook, küçük ve orta ölçekli işletmelerin de ülke ekonomisinde önemli fırsatlar yarattığını belirtti. Cook, yeni merkezlerle geliştiricilere ve işletmelere eğitim, teknoloji kaynakları ve Apple uzmanlarına doğrudan erişim sağlamayı hedeflediklerini ifade etti. Apple'ın açıkladığı plan, Türkiye'de yazılım geliştirme ve ileri üretim teknolojileri alanlarında yeni eğitim imkanları oluşturmayı amaçlıyor. Ancak yatırımın toplam finansal büyüklüğü, yaratacağı istihdam ve merkezlerin kesin öğrenci kapasiteleri henüz açıklanmış değil.

news.title: At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
news.summary: The Atlantic crossing to Spain's Canary Islands remains dangerous for migrants seeking a better life
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
news.summaryTr: The Atlantic crossing to Spain's Canary Islands remains dangerous for migrants seeking a better life
news.articleText: At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal - Published At least 39 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports. The interior ministry said one person had been rescued, but the number of people still missing was yet to be established. The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands. Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands between January and May 2026, the highest toll among the routes it monitors. Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told the AFP news agency that all the bodies recovered by Sunday evening were Senegalese. The nationalities of other people on board was yet to be established, as search operations continued. Four bodies were recovered on Monday morning in an advanced state of decomposition and buried following a collective funeral prayer organised by the fire service. Rescue teams are searching along a 25km (15-mile)- stretch of coastline, but operations have been complicated by difficult access and strong ocean currents, which are pushing bodies further south. Authorities say 24 of the 39 victims have been identified and their bodies returned to their families, while 11 others are still awaiting identification. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has expressed his condolences to the victims' families and urged Senegalese nationals not to risk their lives on the dangerous sea crossings. In a statement posted on X, he pledged to intensify efforts to dismantle the networks organising the journeys. "We will relentlessly continue the fight against those who organise these crossings and the work that gives our young people reasons to hope here," he said. The tragedy comes amid renewed concerns over the dangers facing migrant attempting to reach Europe by sea. Walking Borders estimates that about 21 people died for every 100 who reached the Canary Islands during the period it monitored. Senegalese authorities said they had intercepted another boat, on Friday, carrying 142 migrants attempting to reach Spain. Those on board included 23 women, two babies and two other children. Police said the group comprised nationals of Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea and Nigeria. Meanwhile, a state of emergency was declared on the Spanish island of El Hierro on Saturday following a surge in migrant arrivals. More than 3,300 people have reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of November, according to local authorities. This amounts to almost a third of the population on the island, one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants arriving from West Africa. Fernando Clavijo, president of the Canary Islands regional government, described the situation as "absolutely unsustainable," reports the Reuters news agency. The route has grown in prominence amid tighter controls and increased cooperation between European countries and North African states, which may have diverted some journeys away from the central Mediterranean. Limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks are among the factors driving people to leave Senegal, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM). For many young people, the prospect of finding work and earning more abroad remains a powerful incentive, despite the risks of crossing the Atlantic in overcrowded boat. Nearly one in four young people in Senegal was unemployed in the second quarter of 2026, according to the country's statistics agency. The figure highlights the challenge facing President Faye's government as it seeks to create jobs for a predominantly young population that overwhelmingly voted for him in the 2024 elections. In a statement on Sunday, Senegal's interior ministry said it would continue efforts to combat people-smuggling networks, including by strengthening cooperation with neighbouring countries. news.title: BİM'in (BIMAS) kârı yüzde 79 arttı! Üçüncü çeyrekte 10,4 milyar TL net kâr
news.summary: BİM, 2026'nın ilk 9 ayında 26,15 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin net kârı yıllık bazda yüzde 79 artarken, üçüncü çeyrek kârı 10,39 milyar TL ile piyasa beklentilerini aştı.

news.titleTr: BİM'in (BIMAS) kârı yüzde 79 arttı! Üçüncü çeyrekte 10,4 milyar TL net kâr
news.summaryTr: BİM, 2026'nın ilk 9 ayında 26,15 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin net kârı yıllık bazda yüzde 79 artarken, üçüncü çeyrek kârı 10,39 milyar TL ile piyasa beklentilerini aştı.
news.articleText: BİM'in (BIMAS) kârı yüzde 79 arttı! Üçüncü çeyrekte 10,4 milyar TL net kâr - BİM, 2026'nın ilk 9 ayında 26,15 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin net kârı yıllık bazda yüzde 79 artarken, üçüncü çeyrek kârı 10,39 milyar TL ile piyasa beklentilerini aştı. BİM Birleşik Mağazalar A.Ş. (BIMAS), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 9 Kasım'da Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, 1 Ocak-30 Eylül 2026 döneminde 26 milyar 151 milyon 834 bin TL net dönem kârı elde etti. BİM, 2025'in aynı döneminde 14 milyar 598 milyon 567 bin TL net kâr açıklamıştı. Böylece şirketin 9 aylık net kârı yıllık bazda yüzde 79 arttı. BİM'in yalnızca 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğindeki net kârı ise 10 milyar 385 milyon 559 bin TL olarak gerçekleşti. Satış gelirleri 720 milyar TL'yi aştı BİM'in ilk 9 aylık hasılatı, geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki 665 milyar 220 milyon 543 bin TL'den 720 milyar 477 milyon 782 bin TL'ye yükseldi. Böylece satış gelirlerinde yıllık bazda yaklaşık yüzde 8 artış kaydedildi. Şirketin esas faaliyet kârı aynı dönemde 11 milyar 356 milyon 187 bin TL'den 18 milyar 301 milyon 878 bin TL'ye yükseldi. FAVÖK ise 2025'in ilk 9 ayında 38 milyar 121 milyon 696 bin TL seviyesindeyken, 2026'nın aynı döneminde 43 milyar 470 milyon 121 bin TL olarak gerçekleşti. BİM'in varlıkları 466,5 milyar TL'ye ulaştı Şirketin toplam varlıkları 2025 yıl sonundaki 420 milyar 296 milyon 721 bin TL'den 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreği sonunda 466 milyar 542 milyon 192 bin TL'ye yükseldi. Aynı dönemde toplam borçlar 212 milyar 575 milyon 121 bin TL'den 242 milyar 966 milyon 440 bin TL'ye çıktı. Özkaynaklar ise 205 milyar 844 milyon 477 bin TL'den 221 milyar 686 milyon 578 bin TL'ye ulaştı. BİM'in fiyat/kazanç (F/K) oranı 13,19, piyasa değeri/defter değeri (PD/DD) oranı 2,07 olarak açıklandı. Şirketin piyasa değeri 457,80 milyar TL seviyesinde bulunuyor. news.title: Action on energy costs is my overriding aim, says Fahnbulleh
news.summary: The energy secretary says reducing bills is key to maintaining public support for climate action.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Action on energy costs is my overriding aim, says Fahnbulleh
news.summaryTr: The energy secretary says reducing bills is key to maintaining public support for climate action.
news.articleText: Action on energy costs is my overriding aim, says Fahnbulleh - Published The energy secretary has stressed that affordability is her "overriding objective", as she said reducing bills would be key to maintaining public support for climate action. Speaking to BBC Panorama, Miatta Fahnbulleh insisted that the government's drive for cleaner power would help to cut energy bills in the long term. But she conceded that the push to reduce carbon emissions was currently "under pressure" amid discontent at rising prices in recent years. It comes as ministers grapple with how to respond to a predicted surge in energy prices in January, expected to mark the biggest rise in bills for four years. - Scientists predict 2026 hottest year on record as climate talks begin - Published10 hours ago - Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week - Published5 hours ago Labour has faced extra political pressure over its climate ambitions since coming to power, as Reform UK rose in opinion polls and the Conservatives under Kemi Badenoch disowned their previous ambition of reaching net zero by 2050. Both opposition parties have taken particular aim at public subsidy schemes designed to boost renewable sources of electricity generation, arguing that the drive for cleaner energy has driven up costs for consumers. UK households currently pay one of the highest rates for electricity in Europe. Bills have increased due to subsidies but also because of the high price of gas (a fossil fuel) driven up by international conflicts. Asked during her Panorama interview what her main task was, Fahnbulleh replied: "With the cost of living biting, affordability is my overriding objective, without a doubt." In the interview, which was recorded last week, and aired on Monday night, she argued that Labour's push for greener electricity was "one of our routes to delivering affordability". "The drive to clean power is about decoupling our dependence on global fossil fuel markets," she added. "Ultimately if we have homegrown renewables, nuclear, that's the way in which we will drive bills in the long term." However, she conceded that struggles over energy affordability were part of the reason the consensus on climate action was "under pressure". "People want to blame net zero for that. Now, I don't believe that's the case. "But I'm very clear that part of the way in which we build and maintain public consent is that we've got to show that this transition, which we have to do on climate grounds, is good for people's pockets." Fire and Floods: Our Extreme Weather The BBC's climate editor, Justin Rowlatt, investigates the impact of the changing climate on our weather. Watch on BBC iPlayer or on BBC One (BBC Two in Northern Ireland) at 20:00 on Monday 9 November. The UK had a record number of heatwaves this summer and suffered successive damaging wildfires, which the Met Office has said was made 130 times more likely by climate change. Just last month, whilst hosting the UK's first summit on wildfires, Andy Burnham acknowledged that as a result of climate change "the summer we've just had is likely to be a more regular situation going forward". But he has also vowed to lead a "cost of living government" and reindustralise the economy. This has prompted some in Westminster to speculate that he could demote climate action to help reduce energy costs in the short-term. His government has dismayed some green activists by diverting funding from the energy department to help meet defence funding targets, including money previously earmarked for energy efficiency schemes. Last month the government approved drilling at the Jackdaw gas field which also prompted criticism from some campaigners, although ministers have sought to argue it will minimise imports of higher emission fuels. A decision is yet to be taken on whether production can begin at Rosebank, the UK's largest known untapped oil field, located off the coast of Shetland. Speaking to Panorama, Fahnbulleh insisted reducing carbon emissions "absolutely is a priority", pointing to this summer's droughts as evidence of the need to tackle global warming. However, she conceded that Labour's target for 95% of electricity generated in Britain to come from clean power sources by 2030 was a "stretch". On Monday, it was reported that the government is considering weakening the electric vehicle mandate requiring car manufacturers to phase out production of petrol and diesel cars by 2035. This could prove a blow to not only the country's climate targets but the UK's claim to be providing leadership on the issues just as ministers head to Turkey for COP31, the UN's climate summit. - Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week - Published5 hours ago Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.

news.title: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
news.summary: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
news.summaryTr: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
news.articleText: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published One of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry's most important figures has been accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, prompting an investigation. US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. On Sunday, Huang admitted, external to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. US tech giant Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, has opened an independent investigation into the reports. The firm said it does not believe US national security had been compromised - and added that Huang was committed to continuing to lead the company. Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters. Who is Alice Huang and what do we know about the affair? US officials believed that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reported, external. Her current whereabouts are unknown. Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed between March and November 2023. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked. However, the BBC understands Megaspeed is under investigation by the Singapore government regarding previous allegations that the company was circumventing US sanctions on the export of Nvidia's high-end chips. The BBC has contacted Megaspeed for comment. The company told the New York Times last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation. Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking". It remains unclear what, if any, intelligence Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly gathered and passed to Beijing. She did not respond to the paper's request for comment. When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not. "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC. China has rejected the spying allegations. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters on Monday at a regular daily press briefing: "We have already responded to this. The allegations about Chinese spies are entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China." The New York Times reported in late October that Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence alleging Alice Huang was spying on China's behalf. Asked by reporters on Sunday whether he wished he had "acted on the intelligence", Trump responded: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honourable guy." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, refused to comment when asked about Huang. Last spring, the secretary of state reportedly oversaw the drafting of a memo that warned the Trump administration about Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman, according to the New York Times. Why does it matter? Nvidia is at the heart of US and China's AI race, which is why the billionaire's affair has sparked national security fears among American lawmakers. Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities. The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips. Since 2022, the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security. This means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero. Huang has engaged in shuttle diplomacy between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way. Sunday's revelations may explain why Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China. Who is Jensen Huang? Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University. Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia. Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan and once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech", he has a reputation as a workaholic and perfectionist with incredibly high standards for his staff. He has an estimated fortune of $155bn (£115bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. "Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today. Huang has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Huang. Trump said he had not spoken to the Nvidia boss since news of the investigation emerged. "I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what's going on," Trump told reporters, adding that he had "done an amazing job for our country". What is Nvidia and how important is it? Founded by Huang and fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993, the company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games. Eventually it changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates. Huang rescued Nvidia from bankruptcy on more than one occasion, and took risks on AI a long time before the rest of the world did, effectively building the infrastructure from scratch. "Today when we think of that, we think of these giant data centres - none of that existed. There were no customers for the stuff he was building. In fact his first customer was Open AI at the time they had 30 people - he actually gave it to them, he donated it to them," Witt told the BBC. Every notable tech company building AI tools and infrastructure, including Amazon, Meta, Google, and Microsoft, now use Nvidia chips. Currently worth $4.5tn (£3.4tn), Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies ever. For now, the firm's board appears to have little appetite for removing Huang, saying in a statement on Sunday that they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team". Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake. There is no public succession plan for the 63-year-old. He has often said he hopes to continue in the role for decades, and Bloomberg reports he has created an informal leadership structure around him unlike a traditional company's hierarchy. His children, Spencer and Madison, and son-in-law Nico Caprez work at Nvidia in senior roles. Who is Jensen Huang's wife? Huang met his future wife Lori Mills at Oregon State University while studying electrical engineering in the early 1980s. The pair were lab partners. They married in 1985, about eight years before he co-founded Nvidia, and have two children, Madison and Spencer. In 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation. The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn. Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University. Witt told the BBC that Huang has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, adding: "That's very important to him". "He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," he added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad." Additional reporting by Tom McArthur in London, Ayeshea Perera and Tessa Wong in Singapore and Helen Davidson in Sydney - Published21 September
