news.articleText: Borsada bir hissede tedbir kararı: Kredili işlem ve açığa satış yasağı geldi - Borsa İstanbul, Volatilite Bazlı Tedbir Sistemi (VBTS) kapsamında Kartonsan (KARTN) paylarına yönelik tedbir kararı aldı. Hissede açığa satış ve kredili işlem yasağı 10 Kasım'da başlayacak. Borsa İstanbul, Kartonsan Karton Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. (KARTN) paylarına yönelik tedbir uygulanacağını duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) 9 Kasım 2026 tarihinde yayımlanan açıklamaya göre, Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK) kararı doğrultusunda Volatilite Bazlı Tedbir Sistemi (VBTS) kapsamında KARTN payları açığa satışa ve kredili işlemlere konu edilemeyecek. Tedbir, 10 Kasım 2026 tarihli işlemlerden seans başında başlayacak ve 9 Aralık 2026 tarihli işlemlerin seans sonuna kadar devam edecek. VBTS nedir? Volatilite Bazlı Tedbir Sistemi, Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören paylarda aşırı fiyat hareketlerinin önüne geçilmesi ve piyasa istikrarının desteklenmesi amacıyla uygulanıyor. Sistem kapsamında hisselere belirli sürelerle açığa satış ve kredili işlem yasağı gibi tedbirler getirilebiliyor.

news.articleText: Doğuş Otomotiv (DOAS) beklentileri karşılayamadı! Şirket 3. çeyrekte zarar etti - Doğuş Otomotiv, 2026'nın ilk 9 ayında 2,05 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin net kârı yıllık bazda yüzde 69 gerilerken, üçüncü çeyrekte 434,1 milyon TL zarar kaydedildi. Doğuş Otomotiv Servis ve Ticaret A.Ş. (DOAS), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 9 Kasım'da Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, 1 Ocak-30 Eylül 2026 döneminde 2 milyar 53 milyon 494 bin TL net dönem kârı elde etti. Doğuş Otomotiv, 2025'in aynı döneminde 6 milyar 554 milyon 183 bin TL net kâr açıklamıştı. Böylece şirketin 9 aylık net kârı yıllık bazda yüzde 69 geriledi. Şirketin yalnızca 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğindeki net sonucu ise 434 milyon 107 bin TL zarar oldu. Satış gelirleri yüzde 24 azaldı Doğuş Otomotiv'in ilk 9 aylık hasılatı, geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki 221 milyar 659 milyon 384 bin TL'den 168 milyar 708 milyon 906 bin TL'ye geriledi. Böylece satış gelirlerinde yıllık bazda yaklaşık yüzde 24 düşüş kaydedildi. Esas faaliyet kârı da aynı dönemde 13 milyar 941 milyon 512 bin TL'den 4 milyar 573 milyon 675 bin TL'ye düştü. Esas faaliyet kârındaki gerileme yüzde 67 oldu. Şirketin FAVÖK'ü ise 2025'in ilk 9 ayında 15 milyar 364 milyon 426 bin TL seviyesindeyken, 2026'nın aynı döneminde 7 milyar 531 milyon 965 bin TL olarak gerçekleşti. Varlıklar ve özkaynaklar geriledi Doğuş Otomotiv'in toplam varlıkları 2025 yıl sonundaki 162 milyar 71 milyon 285 bin TL'den 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreği sonunda 153 milyar 415 milyon 210 bin TL'ye geriledi. Aynı dönemde toplam borçlar 77 milyar 399 milyon 262 bin TL'den 74 milyar 254 milyon 341 bin TL'ye, özkaynaklar ise 83 milyar 477 milyon 96 bin TL'den 78 milyar 6 milyon 705 bin TL'ye düştü. Şirketin piyasa değeri 30,40 milyar TL, PD/DD oranı ise 0,39 olarak açıklandı. DOAS bilançosu beklentileri karşılayamadı Matriks Haber tarafından gerçekleştirilen bilanço anketine 13 aracı kurum katıldı. Ankete göre Doğuş Otomotiv'in üçüncü çeyrek net kârına ilişkin ortalama beklenti 851 milyon 500 bin TL, medyan beklenti ise 842 milyon TL oldu. Şirketin açıkladığı 434 milyon 107 bin TL'lik net zarar, piyasa beklentilerinin oldukça altında kaldı. Böylece DOAS, üçüncü çeyrekte analist beklentilerini karşılayamadı.

Altınay Savunma bilançosu beklentileri aştı Matriks Haber tarafından gerçekleştirilen bilanço anketine bir kurum katıldı. Ankette Altınay Savunma için üçüncü çeyrekte 80 milyon TL net zarar beklentisi bulunuyordu. Şirketin açıkladığı 212 milyon 595 bin TL net kâr, piyasa beklentisinin belirgin şekilde üzerinde gerçekleşti.

news.articleText: Who is the suspected Chinese spy at centre of the Nvidia investigation? US chip giant Nvidia has said it is investigating reports that its CEO Jensen Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, who had been the managing director of Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The New York Times reported that US officials suspect Alice Huang has been working for China's spy agency to collect intelligence. China has denied allegations of Huang being a Chinese spy, calling the allegations "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China." Nvidia says it has no reason to believe its secrets or national security were compromised, but will "examine all available information". Asia reporter Tessa Wong explains what we know about Alice Huang, and her links to Jensen Huang.

news.summary: Binance’s pledge to cover all user losses helped contain the fallout from the $6.3 billion hack, analysts said.

news.titleTr: Analysts see no broader ‘contagion’ from $6.3B Binance hack
news.summaryTr: Binance’s pledge to cover all user losses helped contain the fallout from the $6.3 billion hack, analysts said.
news.articleText: Analysts see no broader ‘contagion’ from $6.3B Binance hack Binance’s pledge to cover all user losses helped contain the fallout from the $6.3 billion hack, analysts said. Binance’s pledge to cover user losses from its $6.3 billion hack helped contain the fallout across crypto markets, analysts told Cointelegraph. “There doesn’t seem to be any contagion-type effect from the hack, given that Binance is able to cover the losses using its balance sheet,” Martin Lee, market insights lead at DWF Labs, told Cointelegraph. He said investors turned their focus to the implications of the US midterm elections. Binance’s daily net outflows fell to $458 million in the 24 hours leading to Monday’s publication time, down from $6.1 billion on Nov. 2 after withdrawals resumed, according to DefiLlama. Attackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance hot wallets in the Oct. 29 breach, making it the largest crypto hack to date. Bitcoin (BTC) fell as much as 5.7% over the first five days after the hack, a decline CryptoQuant called “modest” in its Wednesday report . Bitcoin fell roughly 13.6% after the $1.4 billion Bybit hack in 2025 and about 9.9% after the Coincheck hack in 2018. At least 14 of the past 38 hacks CryptoQuant reviewed were followed by steeper Bitcoin declines. Bitcoin’s drawdown after the Binance hack, compared to previous exchange hacks. Source: CryptoQuant Major exchange hacks have previously triggered “short-lived drawdowns that markets later absorbed” as long-term holder demand returned, Lacie Zhang, research lead at Bitget Wallet, told Cointelegraph, adding that the Binance hack does not represent a “structural trend reversal” for crypto markets. Related: Binance hackers had 8-week intrusion window before $6.3B exploit: SEAL Bitfinex analysts say CPI could help confirm a Bitcoin bottom “Much of the hack’s impact now looks priced in,” with Bitcoin currently trading at an “attractive level,” Bitfinex analysts told Cointelegraph. “Confirmation of a market bottom now depends on the Consumer Price Index (CPI) reading due on 10 November, which will shape the Federal Reserve’s next rate decision. Higher bond yields would put pressure on risk assets.” Market participants priced in an 80% chance that the Federal Reserve will raise rates at its Dec. 9 meeting, up from 69% a month earlier, according to the CMEGroup’s FedWatch tool. Bitcoin fell 2.5% over 24 hours to $74,580 as of 1:21 pm UTC on Monday, according to CoinMarketCap. Magazine: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms: Hodler’s Digest

news.title: Thirteen migrants die after boat sinks off Crete
news.summary: The Greek coastguard says it has rescued 18 people, all of whom were Sudanese nationals.

news.titleTr: Thirteen migrants die after boat sinks off Crete
news.summaryTr: The Greek coastguard says it has rescued 18 people, all of whom were Sudanese nationals.
news.articleText: Thirteen migrants die after boat sinks off Crete - Published At least 13 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of the Greek island of Crete. The coastguard said it had rescued 18 people, all of whom were Sudanese nationals. Four of the survivors were taken to hospital, including a toddler. Authorities said it was not immediately clear what caused the deaths, but they believe the boat had been at sea for days and had struggled to reach shore due to strong winds. Crete remains one of several key gateways for migrants attempting to reach Europe from the Middle East and North Africa, with more than 22,000 of the 86,400 sea arrivals so far this year landing in Crete alone. One unnamed coastguard official who spoke to news agency Reuters on condition of anonymity said the survivors were "shivering from the cold". The migrants' boat was spotted by a Moroccan-flagged container ship about 15 nautical miles (28km) off Crete's coast. The Greek coastguard rescued another 187 people in three separate incidents off the coast of Greece on Monday. More than 37,000 migrants have arrived in Greece so far this year, UN figures show, already surpassing the number who arrived in the entirety of 2025. The Greek government has announced plans to deal with the influx, including opening a temporary housing complex near the Cretan capital, Heraklion. Greece was at the heart of Europe's migration crisis in 2015-16, when nearly a million people arrived on its islands, mostly from Turkey. Arrivals later fell as border controls tightened, but crossings from Libya have surged in recent years, particularly among people fleeing conflict in Sudan and seeking better economic opportunities from countries including Bangladesh.

news.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
news.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, the European Union called on the finance industry to write a common rulebook for tokenized securities, Zcash developers seek another reduction in block times and Binance France is closing up shop in the country. EU taps industry to set standards for tokenized securities The European Central Bank, European Commission and European Securities and Markets Authority are seeking nominations for an industry-led group that will draft common standards for holding and settling tokenized securities. Eligible applicants include EU industry associations, global institutions, private firms and fintech companies. They can apply to the European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG) by Nov. 27, with work set to begin in January 2027, according to a release published Monday. The three EU institutions will participate as observers. The group will develop technical and market standards to help companies hold and settle tokenized securities across different distributed ledger technology (DLT) platforms and ensure those platforms can work with existing financial systems. The group aims to produce an initial set of standards by early 2028, according to its mandate. The standards will support Appia, the Eurosystem’s initiative to develop a blueprint for Europe’s tokenized financial markets. The institutions warned that fragmentation could limit the benefits of tokenization and said the group may recommend ways for EU authorities to encourage firms to adopt its standards. In September, the Eurosystem launched Pontes, a system that allows financial institutions to settle wholesale transactions in tokenized assets in central bank money. Zcash devs propose another block time cut days after NU7 upgrade Zcash developers have proposed reducing the blockchain’s target block interval from 25 seconds to 20 seconds, seeking faster transaction confirmations days after activating the NU7 upgrade. On Sunday, developers ValarDragon and Evan Forbes submitted a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal (ZIP) on GitHub, saying that they want the change to be included in the next community poll and considered for the upcoming NU7.1 network upgrade. The reduction would shorten the expected wait for initial transaction confirmations. According to the proposal, this would improve the user experience for point-of-sale payments, exchange deposits and cross-chain swaps. The developers said the change would not increase the network’s overall daily capacity for private transactions. The proposal would also preserve Zcash’s existing issuance schedule, despite blocks being produced more frequently. The proposal comes just days after Zcash’s NU7 upgrade went live. On Friday, the NU7 upgrade was activated on the mainnet, cutting the network’s target block interval from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. The upgrade also introduced a Network Sustainability Mechanism designed to recycle a portion of transaction fees into future mining rewards while preserving Zcash’s 21 million ZEC supply cap. Binance France emails announce closure of accounts Dec. 31 Binance France is closing up shop in the country. Customers have been notified by email during early November, according to media reports. All accounts will be closed on Dec. 31, and any assets left on the exchange will be charged monthly fees starting on Nov. 29, Cryptoast, Crypto Briefing and other media reported on Saturday, citing emails sent to users by Binance. On that date, accounts still maintaining a balance will pay a monthly maintenance fee of 0.025% of the balance, or a minimum of 10 USDC, a stablecoin tracking the US dollar. To avoid fees, withdrawals must be completed by Nov. 29, the exchange said.

news.title: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules
news.summary: The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules
news.summaryTr: The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins.
news.articleText: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins. Opinion by Lissele Pratt, co-founder, Capitalixe Last weekend, the Federal Bureau of Investigation claimed that North Korea was behind the $6.3 billion Binance hack, which analysts are calling the largest heist on record. While I’ve read a lot about the scale of this heist, far less has been said about what went right. Because while it is true that the perpetrators stole $6.3 billion, they haven’t actually been able to hold on to a significant proportion of those takings. $2.85 billion of the funds has been frozen. The reason for this comes down to what the stolen money was comprised of. Of that $2.85 billion, 94% was held in stablecoins. While this hack was terrible news all around, it did show that centralized control, oftentimes criticized by crypto purists, might actually be one of the strongest tools we have against crypto crime. Because, unlike other assets, stablecoins can be frozen by their issuers, giving victims a real chance to stop stolen money reaching the wrong hands. It does, however, raise an uncomfortable question. If private companies have the power to freeze billions of dollars in assets, who decides when they should be allowed to use it? The United Kingdom now has the opportunity to do just that. The race to get rid of stablecoins To get an idea of just how much the freeze mattered, you just have to look at what the hackers did within the first hour of their heist. Related: Binance, Polymarket seek Polygon hard fork to recover $6.8M in stolen crypto Clearly, they understood that there was a very limited window to move the stablecoins before anyone could stop them. So that’s exactly what they did. What was frozen from the Binance hack. Source: Elliptic Less than an hour after the hack began, they had already sold $325 million worth of stolen USDT (Tether’s stablecoin) for Ether. The reasoning behind this was to swap an asset that could be frozen with one that could not. Luckily, stablecoin issuers were quick to act, with Tether’s first major freeze coming just 37 minutes after the stolen funds reached the hackers’ main wallet, and Circle following three minutes later, blocking the movement of USDC. Without Tether and Circle intervening, far more of the funds could have ended up beyond their reach. We’re yet to agree on the rules The freeze, to its credit, worked for the most part because a handful of companies decided, in real time, to use it. The problem is that there still isn’t an agreed standard that outlines when a freeze is justified or how quickly the response needs to be, and we’re beginning to see the consequences of not having these answers. For instance, Circle is facing a proposed class action from Drift Protocol investors who allege it failed to freeze around $230 million in stolen USDC after the April hack. Their argument is that Circle could have stopped the money from moving, but didn’t act in time. Meanwhile, Tether is being sued in New York by two businessmen who claim it froze millions of their assets months before a seizure warrant existed. It’s important to mention that Tether has responded to this case, calling these allegations baseless. Working in payments and banking, it’s not uncommon for me to see traditional banks freeze money and accounts. Due to this, you may argue that if a bank can do this frequently, why shouldn’t a stablecoin issuer be able to? Stablecoin freeze timeline. Source: CertiK My argument isn’t that they shouldn’t. But banks don’t get to decide they want to freeze assets out of nowhere. There’s usually a legal trigger behind their decision, as well as a way to challenge it. Stablecoin issuers now hold the same power while having to act faster and across borders. So it’s about time they’re given some structure. Britain can fix this There is, however, a caveat with regulating stablecoin issuers. Tether and Circle, two of the largest issuers, aren’t based in the UK, so British regulators can’t simply tell them what to do. Related: Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool What Britain can control, though, is which stablecoins UK customers are allowed to buy, and they’ve already begun doing so. In June, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) published its cryptoassets regime. Under it, UK trading platforms must carry out due diligence and publish a disclosure document before they list a coin, and that includes stablecoins issued overseas. It comes into force on 25 October 2027. The Bank of England is finalizing its Code of Practice for systemic stablecoin issuers by the end of this year. It covers stablecoins used widely enough for payments to matter to UK financial stability. Neither framework establishes the clear obligations around freezing stolen funds that I believe are necessary. But both are still taking shape, giving the UK the perfect opportunity to address this gap now, rather than trying to retrofit new requirements later. Two conditions for a UK listing So here’s a solution that I believe would work. Before a stablecoin can be sold on a UK platform, its issuer should have to agree to two conditions. The first being that it is contactable and ready to act. Tether and Circle did exactly that last week, but the victim was the world’s biggest exchange. A small UK platform should get the same response. I work with a number of smaller crypto businesses that don’t have Binance’s profile or a direct line to Tether. Under the current system, they’re the ones most likely to be left waiting. The second is that there needs to be a clear timetable for what happens next. If an issuer freezes funds, it should notify the National Crime Agency that same day. The freeze should then expire if there hasn’t been a court order put out to keep the wallet frozen. Neither of these are extremely controversial takes. They’d give law enforcement a chance to intervene when money is stolen and also protect people from having their assets frozen indefinitely, without legal grounds. The Binance hack has shown us that stablecoins can give victims of crypto crime a chance to stop stolen money before it’s gone for good. That shouldn’t be a privilege reserved only for the world’s biggest exchanges. Magazine: Can decentralized phone networks power the AI revolution?

Related: Binance, Polymarket seek Polygon hard fork to recover $6.8M in stolen crypto Clearly, they understood that there was a very limited window to move the stablecoins before anyone could stop them. So that’s exactly what they did. What was frozen from the Binance hack. Source: Elliptic Less than an hour after the hack began, they had already sold $325 million worth of stolen USDT (Tether’s stablecoin) for Ether. The reasoning behind this was to swap an asset that could be frozen with one that could not. Luckily, stablecoin issuers were quick to act, with Tether’s first major freeze coming just 37 minutes after the stolen funds reached the hackers’ main wallet, and Circle following three minutes later, blocking the movement of USDC. Without Tether and Circle intervening, far more of the funds could have ended up beyond their reach. We’re yet to agree on the rules The freeze, to its credit, worked for the most part because a handful of companies decided, in real time, to use it. The problem is that there still isn’t an agreed standard that outlines when a freeze is justified or how quickly the response needs to be, and we’re beginning to see the consequences of not having these answers. For instance, Circle is facing a proposed class action from Drift Protocol investors who allege it failed to freeze around $230 million in stolen USDC after the April hack. Their argument is that Circle could have stopped the money from moving, but didn’t act in time. Meanwhile, Tether is being sued in New York by two businessmen who claim it froze millions of their assets months before a seizure warrant existed. It’s important to mention that Tether has responded to this case, calling these allegations baseless. Working in payments and banking, it’s not uncommon for me to see traditional banks freeze money and accounts. Due to this, you may argue that if a bank can do this frequently, why shouldn’t a stablecoin issuer be able to? Stablecoin freeze timeline. Source: CertiK My argument isn’t that they shouldn’t. But banks don’t get to decide they want to freeze assets out of nowhere. There’s usually a legal trigger behind their decision, as well as a way to challenge it. Stablecoin issuers now hold the same power while having to act faster and across borders. So it’s about time they’re given some structure. Britain can fix this There is, however, a caveat with regulating stablecoin issuers. Tether and Circle, two of the largest issuers, aren’t based in the UK, so British regulators can’t simply tell them what to do. Related: Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool What Britain can control, though, is which stablecoins UK customers are allowed to buy, and they’ve already begun doing so. In June, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) published its cryptoassets regime. Under it, UK trading platforms must carry out due diligence and publish a disclosure document before they list a coin, and that includes stablecoins issued overseas. It comes into force on 25 October 2027. The Bank of England is finalizing its Code of Practice for systemic stablecoin issuers by the end of this year. It covers stablecoins used widely enough for payments to matter to UK financial stability. Neither framework establishes the clear obligations around freezing stolen funds that I believe are necessary. But both are still taking shape, giving the UK the perfect opportunity to address this gap now, rather than trying to retrofit new requirements later. Two conditions for a UK listing So here’s a solution that I believe would work. Before a stablecoin can be sold on a UK platform, its issuer should have to agree to two conditions. The first being that it is contactable and ready to act. Tether and Circle did exactly that last week, but the victim was the world’s biggest exchange. A small UK platform should get the same response. I work with a number of smaller crypto businesses that don’t have Binance’s profile or a direct line to Tether. Under the current system, they’re the ones most likely to be left waiting. The second is that there needs to be a clear timetable for what happens next. If an issuer freezes funds, it should notify the National Crime Agency that same day. The freeze should then expire if there hasn’t been a court order put out to keep the wallet frozen. Neither of these are extremely controversial takes. They’d give law enforcement a chance to intervene when money is stolen and also protect people from having their assets frozen indefinitely, without legal grounds. The Binance hack has shown us that stablecoins can give victims of crypto crime a chance to stop stolen money before it’s gone for good. That shouldn’t be a privilege reserved only for the world’s biggest exchanges. Magazine: Can decentralized phone networks power the AI revolution?

news.titleTr: Strategy buys 1,036 Bitcoin as BTC holdings climb to 850,364
news.summaryTr: Strategy bought $81.9 million in Bitcoin last week while spending $188.3 million repurchasing STRC preferred shares, according to its latest SEC filing.
news.articleText: Strategy buys 1,036 Bitcoin as BTC holdings climb to 850,364 Strategy bought $81.9 million in Bitcoin last week while spending $188.3 million repurchasing STRC preferred shares, according to its latest SEC filing. Strategy bought 1,036 Bitcoin for $81.9 million last week, bringing its holdings to 850,364 BTC. The company paid an average of $79,012 per BTC last week, according to its Monday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Strategy said it paid a total of $64.16 billion for its Bitcoin holdings, at an average price of $75,456 per coin. Its holdings now account for roughly 4.05% of Bitcoin’s maximum 21 million supply. Since the start of October, Strategy has spent about $1.06 billion buying back its STRC preferred shares, nearly five times the $219.7 million it spent on Bitcoin over the same period. Strategy spends $188.3 million on STRC buybacks Strategy raised $283.8 million in net proceeds last week by selling about $2.05 million shares of tis common stock (MSTR) through its at-the-market offering program. Strategy used $188.3 million of those proceeds to repurchase about 1.89 million STRC shares, following $208.2 million in buybacks the previous week. It spent $81.9 million on Bitcoin and allocated another $13.6 million to its USD Cash balance. Related: Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends for four preferred stocks Strategy’s separate US dollar reserve fell to $4.77 billion from $4.79 billion after the company drew $21.1 million to pay dividends on its preferred stock. Its USD Cash balance rose about 10% to $146.2 million from $132.7 million. The latest Bitcoin purchase follows Strategy’s acquisition of 811 BTC for $65.5 million the previous week. Strategy’s common stock fell 3% to $125 in Monday’s premarket trading, while its STRC preferred shares edged down 0.06% to $99.7, according to Yahoo Finance. news.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

news.articleText: Release Number 9322-26 CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Clearing and Risk today issued a no-action letter addressing whether derivatives clearing organizations may use trust companies to conduct daily settlements with clearing members. According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

news.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. news.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
news.articleText: Release Number 9315-26 CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws. The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law. “Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.” This action reflects the CFTC’s firm commitment to maintaining its exclusive jurisdiction over CFTC-registered prediction markets. The CFTC continues to draw a clear line: if a state challenges the lawful operation of a derivatives exchange, the Commission will protect federal sovereign interests. The Commission has also initiated legal proceedings against nine other states and has submitted briefs in four federal courts of appeal and one state supreme court. -CFTC-

items.title: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
items.summary: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.

items.titleTr: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
items.summaryTr: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
items.articleText: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud - Published A civil servant who secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud. Kashim Chowdhury, from east London, had five government jobs that overlapped in the spring of 2023. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money. The prosecution accused the 56-year-old of ''deliberate, intentional dishonesty'' and of ''exploiting the system''. After seven hours of deliberation, the jury unanimously found Chowdhury guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by a failure to disclose. The judge said Chowdhury faced a ''very significant custodial sentence''. He added he was refusing bail because of the significance of the crime and for Chowdhury's own wellbeing. 'Abused trust' "This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty," said Sarah Melo, specialist prosecutor at the CPS Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate. "He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing." A Defra spokesperson said Chowdury "abused the trust placed in him as a public servant", adding that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending. Between 2020 and 2023 Chowdhury had eight full-time public sector roles that overlapped and earned him £350,000 in total. The prosecution told the court that on application forms he provided inaccurate information about his employment status and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already a civil servant. Once he secured the roles he didn't tell his employers he was working elsewhere. He was allowed to work entirely from home because he told his employers he was caring for his mother, whom he lived with in east London. She had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. But rather than reduce his workload to look after her, he kept taking on new jobs. In the spring of 2023, when his mother was a few months away from death, he had jobs at the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days. Chowdhury said he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment in the past. He was made redundant from a job at the Department for Education in 2013 and was given a diagnosis of PTSD. He said he had not been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time". But the prosecution barrister, Lucy Organ, told the jury: "He's lied to you in evidence, he's lied to you under oath, which demonstrates the level of deceit he has descended to." A succession of his managers told the court about his poor performance. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time". McCartney said that during video calls Chowdhury had his camera switched off blaming technical problems. McCartney said this went on for four to five months. But McCartney said that because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job and remained there for two years. The prosecution argued that he used sick notes to cope with his impossible schedule. In March 2023, he was on sick leave from four of the organisations he worked for. But he kept working at the Home Office and did not tell them he was ill. His line manager at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023. By this point he'd been off sick for three months and she wanted to make a plan to get him back to work. She told the jury that at the start of the call he was coughing a lot and waving tissues up to the camera. She also told the jury that he had been wearing white make-up to try to look ill. Adams told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck." Chowdhury told the jury this was a smear and that he had not been wearing make-up. After the call, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it he blamed a technical error. Adams grew suspicious. ''I believed he was lying,'' she told the jury. She escalated her concerns up the chain at the UKHSA. But his fraudulent behaviour went on for several more months until he left the civil service in September 2023. He was finally caught in 2024 by the government's National Fraud Initiative, which conducts searches of civil service databases such as payroll every two years to look for anomalies. Chowdhury has also been accused by his siblings of bullying their mother into increasing his share of the family home days before she died. In a case at the High Court, Chowdhury's two brothers and sister allege that he put "undue influence" on Faijun Nessa to sign documents that meant he would inherit half of her home. The four-storey, six-bedroom home in east London has been valued at £2.1m. His siblings say their mother could not have understood what she was signing because she was "desperately unwell". In January 2023 she was given a terminal diagnosis of stage four metastatic colorectal cancer. The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed. Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing.

items.title: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results
items.summary: Trump made the claims, without evidence, on Truth Social on Monday.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results
items.summaryTr: Trump made the claims, without evidence, on Truth Social on Monday.
items.articleText: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results - Published US President Donald Trump has questioned the legitimacy of the midterm election results in which Republicans suffered sweeping losses - days after saying he would accept the outcome. "Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong?" Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday. This appeared to contradict what he told the New York Times on election night that he was "absolutely willing" to accept the results. Democrats retook both chambers of Congress in last week's elections. State and local officials across the US said voting had been mostly problem-free. Some key races, including Senate contests in Alaska and Mississippi, have yet to be called. In the Truth Social post, Trump made vague claims about polling, voting "dumps", and "machines" without providing specific evidence of error or wrongdoing. He has previously attempted to cast doubts on the integrity of elections he has lost, although he himself was not on the ballot in the midterms. "We would have won easily if I was on the ballot," Trump told CBS News, the BBC's US partner, after it was confirmed his party had lost both the Senate and the House. As it stands, Democrats have won 54 US Senate seats and 254 US House seats in the midterms, giving them comfortable majorities in both chambers of Congress even as counting continues in some races. The outcome has been clear since election night and Trump told the New York Times then: "We'll, you know, look forward to working with [Democrats]", adding: "We'll probably work something out." He has also offered his own analysis of why Republicans lost, acknowledging on Fox News that the Iran war had contributed to the defeat. "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran but they really probably weren't willing to do the short term consequences of paying more for gasoline - I understand that," he said. Vice-President JD Vance has also blamed the Iran war, which began in February and which has severely disrupted global oil and gas supplies - causing costs to soar, as the reason their party lost the election. In the run-up to the midterms, Trump made claims about widespread voting fraud, despite evidence that it is rare. He and his allies alleged for months that the 2020 presidential election, which he lost to former President Joe Biden, had been rigged against him. His lawyers and allies spent weeks attempting to litigate the results, but courts repeatedly struck them down. The justice department during his administration has made unprecedented attempts to exert more federal control over elections - a power the Constitution primarily delegates to individual states. Days before these midterms, it filed controversial lawsuits in federal courts challenging the count and certification of votes in states like California and Alaska, but judges ruled against them in nearly all instances. Election law experts, state officials, and local elections offices told the BBC they had spent months preparing for a scenario in which the White House or election sceptics questioned the votes' legitimacy. Despite the intense focus around election integrity on both sides of the debate, top state and local election officials have reported a mostly smooth process so far for the 2026 midterms. Extreme weather did force some location closures, and a handful of reported administrative or technical issues slowed the process in some local jurisdictions.

items.title: Nine Zimbabweans caught allegedly trying to leave South Africa to fight in Ukraine
items.summary: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Nine Zimbabweans caught allegedly trying to leave South Africa to fight in Ukraine
items.summaryTr: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.
items.articleText: Nine Zimbabweans caught allegedly trying to leave South Africa to fight in Ukraine - Published Nine Zimbabweans have been arrested in South Africa after they were caught allegedly trying to leave the country to fight in the war between Russia and the Ukraine, police say. The group, aged between 20 and 26, were arrested in and around Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team on Sunday evening. They were caught as they were "preparing to board flights out of the country", authorities added, but their final destination is unclear. They have been charged with contravening South Africa's Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act, which outlaws mercenary activity without government permission. Police said five people were arrested at South Africa's biggest airport, OR Tambo, and another four at a hotel in Bruma, east of Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team that involved Interpol. All nine later appeared in court, according to state prosecutors. The police statement added that the involvement of Interpol and other international law enforcement agencies indicated that the suspects had also allegedly violated laws in their respective home countries, prompting cooperation with South African authorities. They have also not said whether the group allegedly intended to fight for Russia or Ukraine nor provided details of the organisations allegedly involved in facilitating their travel. Citizens of several African countries, including Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, have gone to fight for Russia in Ukraine - some they had been duped and had not realised where they were going. A Ukrainian intelligence assessment estimated earlier this year that more than 1,700 people from 36 countries in Africa have been recruited to fight for Russia. Kenya at the time estimated that 252 citizens had been illegally conscripted in Russia. In March, Foreign Minister Musalia Mudavadi visited Moscow to address the issue. He said at the time that an agreement had been reached to stop recruiting Kenyan nationals. In March, Zimbabwe said that 15 of its nationals had been killed after being recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine, with more than 60 still trapped on the frontlines. The previous month, South Africa secured the return of 17 South Africans who were allegedly tricked into joining the war. In December last year, South African authorities arrested five people, including a journalist, for allegedly recruiting people to join the war. Ukraine has also been recruiting foreign nationals, including from Africa. items.summary: "It destroys people, but we all make our own choices" - Marseille drug-gang members spoke to the BBC.

items.titleTr: Men recruited to French gang as children to kill give rare insight into drug underworld
items.summaryTr: "It destroys people, but we all make our own choices" - Marseille drug-gang members spoke to the BBC.
items.articleText: Men recruited to French gang as children to kill give rare insight into drug underworld A BBC investigation has found one of Europe's most powerful drug gangs in France is recruiting teenage children from across the country to commit kidnap and murder. Known as the "DZ Mafia", the gang won a bloody turf war against a rival group in Marseille during 2023, and is now recruiting from further afield. One member who is in prison awaiting trial after being implicated in several murders told the BBC he was part of a DZ Mafia hit squad. He agrees the killings he has been charged with were "quite shocking". "Attempts in broad daylight, in traffic jams… it can range from going to hit a guy, slap him to taking him in front of his mother and burning him up in a car. I think I have good composure, I handle it fairly well." When challenged over whether he feels regret when carrying out such acts of brutality, he says he feels "guilty in-part" but claims to have no regrets. Like so many teenagers from Marseille, he knew large sums of money could be earned quickly in drug trafficking. Now in his twenties, he admits the environment he entered was a "trap". The BBC's Paris Correspondent, James Waterhouse, reports from Marseille.

items.articleText: Erdoğan'dan emekli maaşları için yeni mesaj: “Mali imkanları oluşturuyoruz” - Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan, fon soruşturmasına ilişkin “Taviz yok” mesajı verirken emeklilerin durumunu iyileştirecek mali imkanlar üzerinde çalışıldığını söyledi. Gabar'da iki yeni sahadan daha olumlu haber geldiğini belirten Erdoğan, petrol üretimi ve enerji hedeflerine ilişkin açıklamalarda bulundu. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan başkanlığında gerçekleştirilen Kabine toplantısının ardından ekonomi gündemine ilişkin açıklamalar yapıldı. Erdoğan, fon soruşturmasının yakından takip edildiğini belirtirken emekli aylıklarına yönelik yeni düzenleme çalışmalarına ve Gabar'daki petrol faaliyetlerine de değindi. Fon soruşturmasında “taviz yok” mesajı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan, fon soruşturmasına ilişkin sürecin yakından takip edildiğini belirterek, “Meseleyi çok sıkı bir şekilde takip ediyoruz. Vatandaşlarımız bize güvenmeye devam etsin” ifadelerini kullandı. Erdoğan'ın açıklaması, soruşturmanın kararlılıkla sürdürüleceği mesajı olarak öne çıktı. Emekli maaşlarına ek zam hazırlığı Kabine toplantısının gündeminde emekli aylıklarına yönelik düzenleme de yer aldı. Erdoğan, emeklilerin ekonomik durumunu iyileştirmeye yönelik çalışmalar hakkında, “Emeklilerimizin durumunu biraz daha iyileştirecek mali imkanları oluşturuyoruz” dedi. Emeklilere enflasyon farkının yanı sıra ek refah payı verilmesine yönelik çalışmalar sürüyor. Hazırlanan taslakların Erdoğan'a sunulmasının ardından düzenlemenin bütçe süreciyle birlikte Meclis gündemine taşınması planlanıyor. Ancak emekli maaşlarına yapılacak olası ek zam oranı ve yeni maaş tutarlarına ilişkin henüz kesin bir rakam açıklanmadı. Gabar'da iki yeni sahadan petrol haberi Erdoğan, Türkiye'nin enerji arz güvenliği ve yerli kaynakların üretime kazandırılması konusunda atılan adımlara da değindi. Karadeniz'de üretilen doğal gazla 4 milyon hanenin ihtiyacının karşılandığını belirten Erdoğan, Osmangazi Gemisi'nin devreye alınmasıyla bu sayının 8 milyona çıkarılmasının hedeflendiğini söyledi. Gabar'daki petrol üretimine ilişkin de açıklamalarda bulunan Erdoğan, bölgede iki yeni sahadan daha olumlu haber geldiğini duyurdu. Gabar'da 75,4 milyon varil Türkiye'nin en kaliteli petrolünün üretildiğini ifade etti. Türkiye'nin enerji sepetini genişletmeye, yerli petrol ve doğal gaz kaynaklarını ekonomiye kazandırmaya yönelik çalışmaların sürdüğünü vurguladı.

items.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
items.summary: The cyber-attack last month saw fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France heated up.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
items.summaryTr: The cyber-attack last month saw fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France heated up.
items.articleText: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking - Published France has accused Iran of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of Iran. He said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding that the country would "implement sanctions at the European level against all those responsible for this attack". The cyber-attack last month saw fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France heated up, which spoilt fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros. Then last week, dozens of supermarkets across seven other European countries were also impacted by a cyber-attack that targeted fridges and freezers. It is not known if the instances are linked. Iran is yet to respond to Barrot's allegations. Barrot said of the attack on France's supermarkets: "It marks the first large-scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people." He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act". France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added. Separately on Monday, the Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as well as his two deputies. Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC. On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets. More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight. Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss. The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe. Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects. In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them. The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight. Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss. The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe. Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects. In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them. The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations. items.summary: The discount chain is continuing to edge towards collapse and is said to be "running on fumes", according to one insider.

items.titleTr: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
items.summaryTr: The discount chain is continuing to edge towards collapse and is said to be "running on fumes", according to one insider.
items.articleText: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow - Published Poundland is unable to buy new stock to fill its shelves after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts. The discount chain is on the brink of collapse with one insider describing it as "running on fumes". It has until Thursday to secure a rescue deal. About £50m has been frozen by its American owner Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning its 600 shops are running out of stock. Pressure is building on Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for £1 last June, after the owner rejected a takeover bid that could have saved the thousands of jobs currently at risk. Gordon Brothers has been approached for comment. Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its creditors until Thursday. Access to funds was limited because of a tension between Gordon Brothers' dual role as both creditor and shareholder, a source said, but added they expected a relaxation of funds in the next two days. Last week, Poundland boss Barry Williams told staff like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4% last week, which included Halloween, but said this was £1.5m ahead of budget. He said the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where the business made losses of £68m. The latest annual accounts have yet to be audited. - Burnham 'ready to support' Poundland staff as retailer faces collapse - Published29 October - Poundland staff protest after chain approach administrators - Published29 October However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture of the business, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading". It said it had provided significant funding to support the company's ability to trade since it acquired the business. It has also made £18m, from a combination of debt interest payments and other fees and charges. On Wednesday, executives from Gordon Brothers will appear before the Business Select Committee with MPs probing whether they are genuinely pursuing a solvent rescue of the business, which has 11,000 employees, and whether every realistic step is being taken to protect jobs and stores. The session is being held in private given commercially sensitive discussions are still under way with bidders. Uncertain future On Thursday, the 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended. If not, Poundland is set to collapse into administration and could be broken up. A source familiar with the sales process said London-based Xyra Group was making "significant progress" in its last minute bid to buy Poundland and could now be the front runner. An extension of Thursday's deadline now seems an increasingly likely scenario. But such a case would be difficult to put forward if Gordon Brothers continues to block funding. One observer remarked "if Gordon Brothers is going in front of that committee, you don't want to be giving the message we're pulling up the drawbridge". Even if a deal is agreed to sell the business as a whole, there is no guarantee a new owner would not reduce the number of stores, but suppliers to Poundland would prefer that outcome to hundreds of sites being sold off to other retailers. There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up stores which could mean continuing employment for many workers. The central issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland trading as a national chain.

items.summary: Apple, Türkiye'de beş ücretsiz geliştirici akademisi, İstanbul'da bir Developer Center ve Ankara'da bir üretim akademisi açacak. İlk merkezlerin 2027'de faaliyete geçmesi planlanıyor.

items.titleTr: Apple'dan Türkiye'ye 7 yeni merkez yatırımı! İlk açılış 2027'de
items.summaryTr: Apple, Türkiye'de beş ücretsiz geliştirici akademisi, İstanbul'da bir Developer Center ve Ankara'da bir üretim akademisi açacak. İlk merkezlerin 2027'de faaliyete geçmesi planlanıyor.
items.articleText: Apple'dan Türkiye'ye 7 yeni merkez yatırımı! İlk açılış 2027'de - Apple, Türkiye'de beş ücretsiz geliştirici akademisi, İstanbul'da bir Developer Center ve Ankara'da bir üretim akademisi açacak. İlk merkezlerin 2027'de faaliyete geçmesi planlanıyor. Teknoloji devi Apple, Türkiye'deki faaliyetlerini genişletmek amacıyla yedi yeni eğitim ve teknoloji merkezi kuracağını duyurdu. 9 Kasım'da açıklanan yatırım planı kapsamında Türkiye genelinde beş Apple Developer Academy, İstanbul'da bir Apple Developer Center ve Ankara'da bir Apple Manufacturing Academy açılacak. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Yazılım geliştirme, girişimcilik ve ileri üretim teknolojilerine odaklanacak merkezlerle Türkiye'deki yazılım geliştiricilerin desteklenmesi ve küçük ve orta ölçekli işletmelerin yapay zeka destekli üretim teknolojilerine erişiminin artırılması hedefleniyor. Apple, yatırımın toplam maliyetini açıklamadı. Şirketin takvimine göre ilk geliştirici akademisi ve İstanbul'daki geliştirici merkezi 2027'de, Ankara'daki üretim akademisi ise 2028'de faaliyete başlayacak. Türkiye'de beş ücretsiz geliştirici akademisi açılacak Apple, önümüzdeki üç yıl içinde Türkiye'nin farklı noktalarında beş Apple Developer Academy kurmayı planlıyor. İlk akademi 2027 yılında İstanbul'da açılacak. Diğer dört merkezin hangi şehirlerde kurulacağı henüz açıklanmadı. Akademilerde öğrencilere ve girişimcilere dokuz ay süren ücretsiz ve yoğun eğitim programları sunulacak. Eğitimlerde kodlama, uygulama tasarımı, pazarlama, proje yönetimi ve yapay zeka teknolojilerine odaklanılacak. Programlarda erişilebilirlik, kullanıcı gizliliği ve sürdürülebilirlik konuları da ele alınacak. Apple, akademilerden önümüzdeki yıllarda binlerce öğrencinin yararlanabileceğini belirtiyor. Ancak başvuru tarihleri, kabul koşulları ve kontenjanlar henüz duyurulmadı. İstanbul, Apple'ın geliştirici merkezleri arasına katılacak Apple, 2027 yılında İstanbul'da bir Apple Developer Center da açacak. Merkez, profesyonel yazılım geliştiricilere ve teknoloji girişimlerine yönelik hizmet verecek. Geliştiriciler burada Apple uzmanlarıyla birlikte çalışma, yeni teknolojileri deneyimleme ve uygulamalarını geliştirme imkanı bulacak. Yüz yüze eğitimler, teknik atölyeler, bire bir uzman görüşmeleri ve geliştirici etkinlikleri düzenlenecek. İstanbul'daki merkez, Apple'ın Bengaluru, Berlin, Cupertino, Şanghay ve Singapur'da bulunan geliştirici merkezleri ağına katılacak. Ankara'da yapay zeka ve robotik akademisi kurulacak Yatırım planının üretim teknolojilerine yönelik ayağı ise Ankara'da hayata geçirilecek. 2028 yılında açılması planlanan Apple Manufacturing Academy, Apple'ın ABD dışındaki ilk üretim akademisi olacak. Merkezde özellikle küçük ve orta ölçekli işletmelere yönelik ücretsiz eğitimler verilecek. Programların odağında yapay zeka, makine öğrenmesi, gelişmiş otomasyon, robotik sistemler ve tahmine dayalı bakım teknolojileri bulunacak. Akademide uygulamalı eğitim laboratuvarları, teknoloji gösterimleri, ortak çalışma alanları ve profesyonel gelişim etkinlikleri de yer alacak. Ankara'daki tesisin bir üretim fabrikası olmayacağının altını çizmek gerekiyor. Merkez, Apple cihazlarının üretileceği bir tesis değil; Türkiye'deki işletmelerin ileri üretim teknolojileri konusunda eğitim ve destek alabileceği bir akademi olarak tasarlandı. Tim Cook: Türkiye'deki girişimcileri destekleyeceğiz Apple Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Tim Cook, Türkiye'deki yatırım planına ilişkin açıklamasında şirketin 35 yıldır Türkiye'deki müşterilerine ve topluluklara hizmet verdiğini hatırlattı. Türkiye'deki yazılım geliştiricilerin dünya genelinde kullanılan uygulamalar ürettiğine dikkat çeken Cook, küçük ve orta ölçekli işletmelerin de ülke ekonomisinde önemli fırsatlar yarattığını belirtti. Cook, yeni merkezlerle geliştiricilere ve işletmelere eğitim, teknoloji kaynakları ve Apple uzmanlarına doğrudan erişim sağlamayı hedeflediklerini ifade etti. Apple'ın açıkladığı plan, Türkiye'de yazılım geliştirme ve ileri üretim teknolojileri alanlarında yeni eğitim imkanları oluşturmayı amaçlıyor. Ancak yatırımın toplam finansal büyüklüğü, yaratacağı istihdam ve merkezlerin kesin öğrenci kapasiteleri henüz açıklanmış değil.

items.title: At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
items.summary: The Atlantic crossing to Spain's Canary Islands remains dangerous for migrants seeking a better life
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
items.summaryTr: The Atlantic crossing to Spain's Canary Islands remains dangerous for migrants seeking a better life
items.articleText: At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal - Published At least 39 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports. The interior ministry said one person had been rescued, but the number of people still missing was yet to be established. The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands. Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands between January and May 2026, the highest toll among the routes it monitors. Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told the AFP news agency that all the bodies recovered by Sunday evening were Senegalese. The nationalities of other people on board was yet to be established, as search operations continued. Four bodies were recovered on Monday morning in an advanced state of decomposition and buried following a collective funeral prayer organised by the fire service. Rescue teams are searching along a 25km (15-mile)- stretch of coastline, but operations have been complicated by difficult access and strong ocean currents, which are pushing bodies further south. Authorities say 24 of the 39 victims have been identified and their bodies returned to their families, while 11 others are still awaiting identification. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has expressed his condolences to the victims' families and urged Senegalese nationals not to risk their lives on the dangerous sea crossings. In a statement posted on X, he pledged to intensify efforts to dismantle the networks organising the journeys. "We will relentlessly continue the fight against those who organise these crossings and the work that gives our young people reasons to hope here," he said. The tragedy comes amid renewed concerns over the dangers facing migrant attempting to reach Europe by sea. Walking Borders estimates that about 21 people died for every 100 who reached the Canary Islands during the period it monitored. Senegalese authorities said they had intercepted another boat, on Friday, carrying 142 migrants attempting to reach Spain. Those on board included 23 women, two babies and two other children. Police said the group comprised nationals of Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea and Nigeria. Meanwhile, a state of emergency was declared on the Spanish island of El Hierro on Saturday following a surge in migrant arrivals. More than 3,300 people have reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of November, according to local authorities. This amounts to almost a third of the population on the island, one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants arriving from West Africa. Fernando Clavijo, president of the Canary Islands regional government, described the situation as "absolutely unsustainable," reports the Reuters news agency. The route has grown in prominence amid tighter controls and increased cooperation between European countries and North African states, which may have diverted some journeys away from the central Mediterranean. Limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks are among the factors driving people to leave Senegal, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM). For many young people, the prospect of finding work and earning more abroad remains a powerful incentive, despite the risks of crossing the Atlantic in overcrowded boat. Nearly one in four young people in Senegal was unemployed in the second quarter of 2026, according to the country's statistics agency. The figure highlights the challenge facing President Faye's government as it seeks to create jobs for a predominantly young population that overwhelmingly voted for him in the 2024 elections. In a statement on Sunday, Senegal's interior ministry said it would continue efforts to combat people-smuggling networks, including by strengthening cooperation with neighbouring countries. Only one came home - Published3 September 2023 - Senegalese mother: ‘I found out on social media that my son had died’ - Published27 August 2024 Go to BBCAfrica.com, external for more news from the African continent.
